analysis.title: GS TMT SPEC SALES Informa deal; TSMC GIR raising capex again; SPA preview; DT CMD; TEF questions; BT debate
key_insights: US equities rose on light volumes. The Nasdaq 100 closed at a record and the S&P 500 finished within 0.5% of its peak. Software led, helped by Schneider's $22.6bn PTC deal and strength in e-commerce and cybersecurity. Semis lagged despite gains in Nvidia and Broadcom, and neocloud stocks and Intel fell.

GIR raised its TSMC price target and its 2027E/2028E capex forecasts to US$85bn/US$98bn, from US$78bn/US$82bn. 2026E capex is held at US$64bn. The raise is attributed to equipment inflation and initial Texas expansion costs.

GIR forecasts TSMC revenue growth of 42% YoY in 2026E and 36.9% YoY in 2027E. N2 ramp dilution trims quarterly gross margin to 67.5% in 3Q26 and 67.3% in 4Q26, which GIR says is still better than feared. 4Q26E revenue is forecast to grow 11.0% QoQ.
GIR sees TSMC monthly capacity reaching 200kwpm for N3 and 140kwpm for N2 by end-2027E, and 220kwpm for N3 and 200kwpm for N2 by end-2028E. GIR EPS forecasts for 2026/2027/2028 are 110/150/195.

Sales feedback says TSMC trades at only 17-18x GIR's FY27 EPS of 150, while other AI plays trade above 20x. Sales sees room for the share price to catch up. Focus areas for the analyst meeting are the long-term AI growth outlook, long-term capex and US expansion, and competition from Intel, Samsung and Terafab.

SAP preview ahead of 3Q26 results on 21 October: GIR makes no changes to organic CCB assumptions. It expects c.23% organic CCB growth ex-FX in 3Q26, a modest slowdown to a 22% exit rate in 4Q, and FY26 cloud revenue growth of c.24% ex-FX. Both are in line with company guidance. FY26 guidance looks largely de-risked, and 60% of customers have yet to migrate to S/4HANA.

BESI was downgraded on competition from ASML in hybrid bonding. This follows Semianalysis saying ASML is launching a hybrid bonding tool aimed at die-to-wafer rather than wafer-to-wafer first. GS expects it to cause debate on BESI today.

Informa is buying Clarion from Blackstone for £2.24bn, or 11.1x expected 2027 EBITDA. That falls to c.9x with cost synergies and c.8x with cost and revenue synergies. Funding is acquisition financing plus a c.£940m equity raise, and the buyback is paused. The deal is expected to close in Q4 2026, add mid-single-digit EPS in 2027, and keep leverage below 3x at end-2026 and 2.5x at end-2027.

Informa also plans to separate Taylor & Francis, which grows at c.4%. Combined B2B Live Events is expected to grow more than 7%. GS calls the deal sensible, since a faster-growing asset could be funded largely by selling a slower-growing one. Bulls cite scale, more US exposure, lower macro sensitivity and removal of the AI overhang from Taylor & Francis as reasons for a higher standalone Events multiple.

Spanish election: GS is getting questions on Telefonica and Indra. A change of government could alter the state's relationship with the companies. It could lead to a gradual sale of SEPI's 10% stake, since the PP was critical of the stake and intends to divest it. The state would rely more on existing foreign-investment safeguards, and board and management uncertainty could follow.

Deutsche Telekom AI capital markets day: management framed AI mainly as cost and productivity, targeting €1.1bn of gross savings by 2027 and €2.5bn by 2030, plus more than €1bn of AI-enabled revenue led by B2B and sovereign AI. Guidance was not raised and no added margin expansion was committed, citing token costs, wage inflation, scaling investment and German fibre reinvestment. Analysts stayed sceptical in Q&A.

DT management said core telco capex should not structurally increase and larger AI infrastructure projects could be partnered. GS sees near-term cost efficiencies as credible. Revenue monetisation, 6G upside and sustained EBITDA acceleration are longer-term optionality that needs evidence in post-2027 guidance. DT will not block AI agents such as Instinct or Muse and thinks it can feed the agent and ensure it understands network quality.

AI power and funding news: Alphabet is near a $1bn+ nuclear offtake with Constellation. Amazon signed a 20-year, 690MW deal for Calvert Cliffs and Microsoft partnered with Constellation to restart Three Mile Island Unit 1. DeepSeek is close to raising at least $12bn ahead of an early-2027 IPO. Moonshot AI raised at about $50bn and is preparing a Hong Kong IPO in 1Q27 that could raise up to $5bn. OpenAI is in $30bn round talks with UAE funds and BlackRock.

Meta and Microsoft are reportedly cutting internal use of Anthropic's Claude to curb costs and shift staff to in-house AI tools, per The Information. OpenAI launched visual ads alongside image generation results. TikTok is launching an AI shopping assistant with in-app checkout.

Samsung (SEC) is set to raise next year's HBM4 supply price to more than three times the HBM3E price. Samsung Foundry has begun mass production of the Exynos 2700, at volumes 10% above its predecessor. AMD CEO Lisa Su is visiting Seoul to expand AI partnerships and secure memory supply from SEC and SK Hynix.
Hon Hai September sales exceeded TWD$1tr, a first for a Taiwanese company, driven by AI and iPhone momentum. Q3 sales are 107% of consensus.

SpaceX Q3 preview: GS raised its AI segment forecasts for capacity, revenue and margins. It says AI segment estimates still look conservative against the Street over the next 6-18 months, absent a broader AI correction. The note also covers launch cadence and re-usability for the Space segment.

Netflix Q3 preview: shares are down 10% since the 7/16 report, against S&P 500 +3%. GS ties the underperformance to weakening platform trends, with fewer engagement metrics disclosed and mixed third-party data. It also cites investor concern that more capital for IP acquisitions or higher 2027 content spend is needed for differentiation.

BT bought TalkTalk's consumer and wholesale businesses out of administration in a debt-free rescue covering 1.5 million customers. Creditors owed nearly £1.5bn face heavy losses, with Ares expected to recover more than £100m. The CMA is due to report by 19 October. VMO2 criticised the £400m deal as favouring BT.

Brazil's election result was substantially better for the market than expected. EWZ rose 13%, with macro shorts likely squeezed and hedge fund demand against long-only supply in high-beta pockets. Early derivatives flow was dominated by upside chasing in short-dated EWZ calls and monetisation of existing positions.

US trading was quiet, with TMT volumes down 10-20% against 10-day averages and the floor at 4 out of 10 on activity. Long-only funds were slight net sellers, led by macro products, and hedge funds were slight net buyers, led by tech. GS sees no real chasing, but US L/S net leverage is at its lowest since April 2025 and a continued index rise would force investors to buy.

US derivatives saw spot-up, vol-up chasing across indices and skew crushed, especially in short-dated S&P. The vol desk sees room for further upside and likes owning QQQ optionality into earnings. There were some larger vol sellers and a large VIX downside trade.
Other deals: C.H. Robinson agreed to buy RXO for $5.8bn. The FT reported McKesson and CD&R near a $5bn-plus deal for an infusion services provider, and OPCH rose 20% after hours.
